items.t: OMV's Upgraded 2026 Guidance Meets a Cluster of Cautious Analysts
sum: OMV has raised its sights for next year, lifting its 2026 outlook on 29 October to assume an average realised gas price of around EUR 45/MWh and a European refining reference margin of roughly USD 25/bbl. The same release carried the group's third-quarter figures, and they were robust: CCS operating profit before special items jumped 68% to EUR 2.12bn, on revenue from continuing operations of EUR 8.96bn.

Those two disclosures — the upgraded assumptions and the earnings leap — explain why the stock has become a battleground for analysts. The quarter's strength rested on a favourable market environment and markedly wider refining margins, with adjusted CCS operating profit reaching EUR 2,117m. Whether that can be repeated is now the central question for investors, and the rating houses are answering it in strikingly different ways.

The most recent moves came yesterday, when two brokerages both cut OMV to "Neutral" from "Outperform" — yet pulled their price targets in opposite directions. ODDO BHF trimmed its target to EUR 74 from EUR 75, pairing the softer stance with a slightly lower valuation. Erste Biuro Maklerskie went the other way, lifting its target to EUR 75 from EUR 48. The combination leaves shareholders in an awkward spot: a higher valuation can arrive alongside a more guarded recommendation.

A week earlier, Morgan Stanley had taken a dimmer view still, downgrading OMV to "Underweight" while raising its price target to EUR 67 from EUR 65.50. That cut, too, came without a reduction in target. With the shares at EUR 73.40, the stock is trading above all three published targets — a signal that the market is already pricing in more than the analysts are formally willing to endorse.

The refining margin is the operative test. OMV credited the strong third quarter to benign market conditions and significantly higher refining margins, and the raised 2026 assumption of USD 25/bbl suggests management expects much of that tailwind to persist. If margins hold at supportive levels, the group could sustain its elevated earnings power for longer, giving investors an operational reason to look past the cautious ratings.
Should margins retreat sharply, the same driver turns against the company.

items.t: OMV's Raised Guidance Cuts Both Ways as Rating Downgrades Pile Up
OMV stock faces mixed signal after 68% Q3 profit jump
OMV's 68% Earnings Jump Meets a Wall of Neutral Ratings
sum: Two brokerage houses moved on OMV on the same day, and the coincidence says more than either note alone. Oddo BHF and Erste Biuro Maklerskie both cut the Austrian oil and gas group from "Outperform" to "Neutral" — yet they arrived at that verdict from opposite directions on price.

Oddo trimmed its target to €74 from €75, so recommendation and valuation moved in step. Erste went the other way on the number, lifting its target to €75 from €48 while still stepping down to Neutral. The two new targets now sit within a euro of each other, a striking convergence given how far apart the previous ones were. That alignment is what gives the twin downgrades their weight; a single target change in isolation would carry far less signal.
At €72.60, the shares trade below both fresh targets, implying only modest headroom if the analysts hold their ground.

What keeps the stock interesting is valuation. Consensus for 2026 puts OMV on a price-to-earnings ratio of 7.03 and a dividend yield of 6.75% — the lowest multiple and the highest yield anywhere in the ATX, Vienna's benchmark index. Those figures offer a counterweight to the cautious ratings, but only conditionally: the low multiple supports the stock if the earnings materialise, and the yield only pays off if the distribution actually lands.

The shares have already climbed 54% since the start of the year. After a run of that size, the two notes raise the bar for further gains. A more convincing buying case would need either rising estimates or a more attractive entry point.

The neutral camp is not the only voice. HSBC went further on 3 November, setting OMV to "Reduce" with a €66 target — below the current share price. That stance sharpens the question investors now face: the earnings momentum is real, but is it durable?

OMV reported third-quarter 2026 CCS operating profit before special items of €2.1bn, up 68%. Whether that improvement can be repeated is the crux. A benign scenario has the operating strength continuing under the market conditions the company itself expects.

sum: BlackRock disclosed on 2 November a total stake of 5% in OMV, pushing the holding past the relevant reporting threshold. The position is not made up solely of directly held shares: voting rights from stock accounted for 4.53%, with a further 0.47% held through financial instruments.

The disclosure lands as OMV's equity trades at 70.45 EUR — above the target prices set by two of the banks tracking it. That gap between market price and analyst targets captures the central debate now surrounding the Austrian energy group: whether the refining windfall behind its latest quarter can be repeated, or whether it marks a peak.

Roughly two weeks ago OMV reported a sharp increase in earnings for the third quarter of 2026. Adjusted CCS operating profit rose 68% to EUR 2.12 billion, according to company figures, with the result before special items reaching EUR 2,117 million. CCS net profit came in at EUR 1,153 million.

The headline number conceals sharply divergent fortunes across the three divisions. Fuels delivered the largest contribution and the steepest percentage gain, lifting adjusted operating profit 172% to EUR 1.12 billion. Energy added 51% to EUR 936 million. Chemicals moved the other way, with earnings falling 72% to EUR 63 million.

Management attributed the overall strength to higher refining margins and a favourable market environment in Energy, with high utilisation rates providing an additional lift in Fuels. Those same drivers are now the pivot on which the investment case turns.

Analyst reaction has been cautious even as price targets drift higher. BNP Paribas, according to media reports, confirmed its "Neutral" rating on 4 November while raising its target from EUR 64 to EUR 70 — a nod to a more attractive valuation, paired with a stance that stops short of enthusiasm.

Morgan Stanley moved the other way on rating. Analyst Guilherme Levy cut OMV from "Equal Weight" to "Underweight" on Thursday, per media reports, while lifting his target from EUR 65.50 to EUR 67.00. The downgrade followed the quarterly report and its widely diverging divisional results. The timing is telling: the scepticism is not about the quarter just delivered but about what follows it.

OMV Lifts Refining Outlook and Capex as Analysts Split on the Stock
sum: OMV has raised its planned organic investments to roughly EUR 3.5 billion, the company said on 29 October, pairing the higher spending with an upgraded view of European refining economics. The Austrian energy group now expects the European refinery reference margin to average around USD 25/bbl in 2026, up from a previous assumption of about USD 20/bbl.

That revision landed alongside third-quarter 2026 figures reported roughly two weeks ago. Clean CCS operating profit before special items came in at EUR 2.12 billion, a jump of 68% from the same quarter a year earlier. Management credited the refining business, where strong margins and high utilisation underpinned the Fuels division, while Chemicals delivered a weaker performance.

The company's full-year Brent assumption for 2026 was also lifted to above USD 95/bbl. On the growth side, CEO Emma Delaney put completion of the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea at 89% in an interview with APA. First gas is expected in the first half of 2027, and Reuters reported on 29 October that OMV anticipates an annual profit contribution of around EUR 500 million from the venture.

Analyst reaction has been mixed in both direction and conviction. HSBC on Tuesday reportedly lifted its price target to EUR 66 from EUR 63 while keeping its "Reduce" rating, leaving a more generous valuation attached to a cautious recommendation. UBS took a different line after the quarterly release on 30 October, raising its target to EUR 79 from EUR 77 and maintaining a "Buy" stance.

Morgan Stanley moved the other way. The US bank reportedly downgraded OMV to "Underweight" on Friday and set a price target of EUR 67, without giving a reason in the report. The shares slipped 0.7% that session to close at EUR 71.60.

Ownership disclosures added another thread. BlackRock reported a total position of 5.00% of OMV voting rights about a week ago, crossing the 5% notification threshold. Shares accounted for 4.53% of that total, with financial instruments making up the remaining 0.47% — meaning the stake is not composed solely of directly held equity.

OMV Raises Refining Guidance as Chemicals Division and Analyst Downgrade Cloud the Picture
sum: OMV has lifted its full-year refining margin forecast, a move that lands alongside a mixed third-quarter scorecard and a fresh broker downgrade that sent the stock slightly lower on Friday. The Austrian energy group did not, however, offer any guidance for 2027.

The upgraded outlook rests on a market that remains tight. CEO Emma Delaney expects low fuel inventories to keep propping up strained refining markets, giving the margin picture continued support. Shares shed 0.7% on Friday to close at 71.60 euros.

Results for the third quarter of 2026, published roughly two weeks ago, laid bare the diverging fortunes of OMV's businesses. Clean CCS operating profit before special items climbed 68% to 2.12 billion euros, a figure Reuters reported came in broadly in line with market expectations.

Refining did the heavy lifting, with the margin rising to 37.50 US dollars per barrel. Chemicals told a different story: operating profit in that division fell to 63 million euros, a result that disappointed. Clean CCS earnings per share for the quarter reached 3.54 euros.

The raised refining forecast sits within a broader 2026 outlook. OMV lifted its projection for the European refining indicator margin to around 25 US dollars per barrel, and it also assumes a Brent price above 95 US dollars per barrel alongside organic investments of roughly 3.5 billion euros. All of these are full-year expectations rather than results already booked.

Morgan Stanley moved OMV to "Underweight" from "Equal-weight" on Friday, according to media reports, while simultaneously raising its price target to 67.00 euros from 65.50 euros. The two adjustments pulled in opposite directions, and the new target still sits below the closing price of 71.60 euros. The downgrade coincided with Friday's share decline, though it has not been established as the sole cause.

Away from the quarterly numbers, the investment decision on a planned recycling project in Vienna remains outstanding. OMV said no final go-ahead has been given for "Projekt Schleie," a downstream initiative reported on Wednesday. The facility would handle mechanical and chemical recycling of non-hazardous plastic waste, with environmental impact assessment documents citing a planned processing capacity of up to 200,000 tonnes per year.

sum: OMV stock traded at EUR 71.60 on Lang & Schwarz at 11:41 CET on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The weekend snapshot followed a week shaped by stronger third-quarter earnings and a higher investment allocation at OMV Petrom.

OMV reported its third-quarter results on October 29. In the company's official results release, clean CCS operating result rose 68 percent year on year to EUR 2.117 billion. Clean CCS net income attributable to parent shareholders reached EUR 1.153 billion, while operating cash flow increased to EUR 2.199 billion.

Fuels supplied the largest contribution, with clean CCS operating result of EUR 1.124 billion. Energy contributed EUR 936 million. Chemicals was the weak point, with clean operating result falling to EUR 63 million from EUR 222 million in the prior-year quarter.

On Friday, November 6, OMV Petrom shareholders approved a RON 969 million increase in the 2026 investment budget to RON 9.978 billion, according to Ziarul Financiar. The additional spending is focused mainly on Neptun Deep, while the project's estimated total cost for OMV Petrom remains about EUR 2 billion.

The Exploration and Production budget rises 22 percent to RON 6.706 billion. Refining and Marketing spending falls 1 percent to RON 2.455 billion, while Gas and Energy spending increases 7 percent to RON 561 million. The decision raises near-term execution spending without changing the stated overall Neptun Deep cost estimate.

OMV has targeted first gas from Neptun Deep in the first half of 2027. The project is central to the group's production outlook, but the higher current-year allocation also highlights the importance of spending timing, foreign-exchange effects and delivery discipline.

OMV's (VIE:OMV) Strong Earnings Are Of Good Quality
sum: OMV Aktiengesellschaft (VIE:OMV) just reported healthy earnings but the stock price didn't move much. Our analysis suggests that investors might be missing some promising details.

Importantly, our data indicates that OMV's profit was reduced by €767m, due to unusual items, over the last year. It's never great to see unusual items costing the company profits, but on the upside, things might improve sooner rather than later. We looked at thousands of listed companies and found that unusual items are very often one-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. Assuming those unusual expenses don't come up again, we'd therefore expect OMV to produce a higher profit next year, all else being equal.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Unusual items (expenses) detracted from OMV's earnings over the last year, but we might see an improvement next year. Because of this, we think OMV's earnings potential is at least as good as it seems, and maybe even better! The Bet OMV Holders Made
sum: If you only glanced at OMV headlines over the past year, the story looked messy, with decarbonization bets on green hydrogen sitting alongside geopolitical setbacks in oil and gas. Holding OMV over the past year would have returned 65.7%, including dividends. If you had been weighing that decision back in early November 2025, what within the bullish and bearish cases on record might have justified taking that risk, and what still looked like a step into the dark?
The shares cost €48.22 at the start of the period. Anyone looking at OMV then had to choose between two very different but plausible futures for the group.

On the bullish side, one camp saw fair value at €62.5, a level that reflected what that view considered a justified price for stronger earnings power. That story leaned on OMV’s push into green hydrogen and chemicals, including early work on a large 140 megawatt electrolyzer.

The bearish narrative pointed to a fair value of €40, again simply the price implied by its own more cautious assumptions. This view stressed decarbonization policies eroding oil and gas demand and the risk that some hydrocarbon assets could eventually be written down.

The clearest new fact was OMV securing a €450 million European Investment Bank loan and moving into electrolyser installation for its 140 MW green hydrogen plant, directly backing the bullish argument that transition projects were real rather than aspirational. Quarterly data pointed the same way. Revenue reached €8,715 million and net income €1,024 million in Q3 2026, with net margin at 11.7%, so profitability improved versus Q3 2025. Taken together, this evidence supported the optimistic case more than the cautious one.

The lesson is simple. When a thesis hinges on decarbonization projects and better margins, do not stop at capex headlines. Track whether funded projects hit construction milestones and whether net margin, not just revenue, moves towards the scenario investors were underwriting.
OMV now trades at €72.9, after a 65.7% gain over the past year. The selected Narrative’s Fair Value sits below that level, so it sees the current quote as already baking in a lot of good news.

OMV stock: Q3 clean CCS result jumps 68% on fuels strength
sum: OMV reported a stronger third quarter on October 29, with the integrated energy group benefiting from higher commodity prices and sharply improved refining margins. In its third-quarter results release, OMV said clean CCS operating result rose 68% from a year earlier to EUR 2,117 million. Clean CCS net income attributable to stockholders of the parent reached EUR 1,153 million, while clean CCS earnings per share nearly doubled to EUR 3.54.

Energy clean operating result increased 51% to EUR 936 million. OMV attributed the improvement mainly to higher realized oil and gas prices, which offset lower sales volumes caused in part by missing liftings in the Middle East amid regional logistics constraints. Hydrocarbon production declined 3% to 294 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day.

Fuels delivered the largest earnings contribution. Its clean CCS operating result climbed to EUR 1,124 million from EUR 413 million in the prior-year quarter. Higher European and Middle Eastern refining margins, strong refinery utilization and a more favorable product mix supported the increase. OMV's European refining indicator margin more than tripled to USD 37.50 per barrel.

Chemicals provided a counterweight. Its clean operating result fell to EUR 63 million from EUR 222 million as benchmark prices weakened and Borouge International contributed EUR 16 million. The figures are clean CCS or clean operating measures where stated and therefore exclude the relevant effects of special items and crude-price changes.

Operating cash flow rose to EUR 2,199 million, while cash flow excluding net working capital effects reached EUR 2,334 million. OMV ended the quarter with net debt of EUR 4,403 million and a leverage ratio of 17%, giving investors a balance-sheet reference as the group continues to fund capital spending and strategic projects.

OMV stock: Q3 clean CCS result rises 68 percent
sum: OMV reported a stronger third quarter on Thursday, October 29, 2026, with higher energy prices and refining margins lifting earnings across its integrated energy business. In its third-quarter results release, OMV said its clean CCS Operating Result increased 68 percent year over year to 2,117 million euros. Clean CCS net income attributable to stockholders of the parent reached 1,153 million euros, up 94 percent, while clean CCS earnings per share rose 95 percent to 3.54 euros.

Sales revenues from continuing operations increased 43 percent to 8,959 million euros. Operating cash flow more than doubled to 2,199 million euros, and cash flow excluding net working capital effects rose 57 percent to 2,334 million euros. OMV said the stronger cash generation also reflected the first Borouge International dividend, while the balance sheet ended the quarter with net debt of 4,403 million euros and a leverage ratio of 17 percent.

The Energy segment's clean Operating Result rose 51 percent to 936 million euros. Higher realized oil and gas prices more than offset lower sales volumes, which OMV linked to logistical constraints and the lack of liftings in the Middle East. Hydrocarbon production was 294 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, down 3 percent from the prior-year quarter.

Fuels delivered the largest improvement. Its clean CCS Operating Result climbed 172 percent to 1,124 million euros as European and Middle Eastern refining margins, utilization rates and the product mix strengthened. OMV's European refining indicator margin more than tripled to 37.50 US dollars per barrel, while European refinery utilization reached 92 percent. Retail contributions were lower because fuel margins weakened after the rise in international oil product quotations.

Chemicals provided a counterweight, with its clean Operating Result falling 72 percent to 63 million euros. OMV cited lower market prices and a weaker contribution from Borouge International, although base chemicals benefited from stronger olefin margins and steam cracker utilization improved to 82 percent.
OMV now expects 2026 organic capital expenditure of around 3.5 billion euros, compared with its previous forecast of around 3.4 billion euros.

OMV and Energie Steiermark Join Forces in Deep Geothermal Energy
sum: - “Tiefenkraft”, a joint project by OMV and Energie Steiermark
- Successful seismic survey campaign lays the groundwork for the next project phase and an exploration well in 2026
- Significant contribution to the heat transition: potential of up to 670 GWh per year by 2037 – covering around 50% of district heating demand in the Graz region
- Next step: exploration well “Petersdorf 2” in St. Marein near Graz

OMV and Energie Steiermark are partnering to advance deep geothermal energy in Styria and actively drive forward the heat transition. At a joint event, the two companies presented “Tiefenkraft”, a joint project by OMV and Energie Steiermark, an initiative to assess the region’s geothermal potential. In the long term, this could deliver up to 670 GWh of geothermal energy annually by 2037, equivalent to around 50% of the district heating supply in the greater Graz area.

Between February and April 2026, a seismic survey was carried out along approximately 900 kilometers of roads used as measurement lines. The data is currently being evaluated and will form the basis for a detailed subsurface model as well as for the next project phases.

Berislav Gašo, OMV Executive Vice President Energy, said: “Harnessing geothermal energy is key to an independent and climate-neutral heat supply in Austria. With our expertise in geology, drilling technology, and project development, we are making a vital contribution to a joint assessment of the region’s geothermal potential with Energie Steiermark and helping lay the foundation for a sustainable heat supply.”

items.t: OMV Shares Brush Record High as Barclays Nods Higher While Hungarian Wash Plants Go Dark
sum: The Austrian energy major finds itself in an unusual spot: its stock is within striking distance of a fresh peak, yet one of its own subsidiaries is shutting down operations to conserve resources. Both developments trace back to the same geopolitical tension that has reshaped European energy markets.

OMV traded at €64.70 on Tuesday, up 2.05 percent on the day and sitting just 0.38 percent below its 52-week high of €64.95. The rally has been relentless — shares have climbed 36.93 percent since the start of the year, powered by a second-quarter earnings report that echoed the strong results posted by peers BP and Shell.

The analyst community is split on what comes next. Barclays raised its price target on Monday from €53 to €57, but held firm on an "Underweight" rating — a signal that the British bank still sees the stock as stretched after its extended run. The firm models earnings per share of €8.98 for 2026 and expects a dividend of €4.53.

That combination of a higher target and a cautious rating tells a nuanced story: Barclays acknowledges the operational improvements but questions whether the share price has run ahead of fundamentals. The market, for its part, appears unbothered by the skepticism. OMV closed Monday at €63.40, up 1.04 percent, and was the most heavily traded name in the ATX Prime — a sign of elevated investor interest around the price-target revision.

Monday's trading also benefited from a broader tailwind: oil prices pulled back as the US opted against further strikes in the Iran conflict, easing geopolitical tensions. That relief rally helped the wider Austrian market, though OMV's own momentum has been building independently of the day-to-day oil swings.

Beneath the surface of the share-price strength lies a reminder of the crisis dynamics at play. OMV Hungária, the group's Hungarian subsidiary, has temporarily shuttered all 130 of its car wash facilities — 73 machine-operated and 57 manual — effective August 3, with no reopening date set. The company cited the strained water and energy situation in Hungary and asked partner businesses to follow suit in reducing consumption.

sum: Public disclosure of inside information according to Art 17 MAR

With respect to the envisaged combination of Borealis, Borouge and Nova under Borouge Group International AG (BGI), OMV has reached an agreement with Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) to adjust the timing of (i) the listing of BGI's shares on the ADX, (ii) the exchange offer to the current free-float shareholders of Borouge plc to receive shares in BGI in exchange for their Borouge plc shares and (iii) the capital increase at the level of BGI. The timing of such ADX listing and exchange offer is anticipated to align with the capital increase at the level of BGI, which is currently expected to take place in 2027, subject to market conditions.

Furthermore, OMV and ADNOC have agreed on a temporary adjustment of the dividend payments from BGI which will result in the reduction of the dividend payable by BGI to OMV and ADNOC in 2026. The expected impact on the OMV dividend would be around EUR 0.6-0.7 per OMV share for the year 2026 (payable in 2027), based on a BGI contribution to OMV’s dividend distribution of USD 250mn instead of the USD 500mn assumed previously.

Despite the fact that ADNOC and OMV currently envisage the BGI listing, the exchange offer and the capital increase at the level of BGI to take place in 2027, ADNOC and OMV have also agreed to discuss certain further shareholder support measures in the year 2027 if required to maintain BGI's investment grade rating.
The foregoing is, inter alia, subject to (i) the implementation of the contractual documentation with ADNOC and (ii) approvals by the corporate bodies of ADNOC.

It is our purpose to reinvent everyday essentials. OMV is an integrated energy, fuels and chemicals company headquartered in Vienna, Austria. Through its businesses, OMV supplies products and solutions that support everyday life and industrial value chains.

In 2025, the company generated revenues of EUR 24 billion and employed around 22,300 people worldwide. OMV's key strategic shareholdings include a 51.2% stake in OMV Petrom and a 50% stake in Borouge International. OMV shares are traded on the Vienna Stock Exchange (OMV) and in the United States on OTCQX (OMVKY, OMVJF).

Europe stocks close higher after investors digested slew of earnings reports
sum: LONDON — European stocks closed marginally higher on Wednesday amid a slew of corporate earnings reports in the region.

The pan-European Stoxx 600 was provisionally 0.1% higher by the end of the session. The U.K.'s FTSE rose almost 1%, as Germany's DAX shed 0.6%, while France's CAC 40 rose 1.2%, and Italy's FTSE MIB adding 0.6%.
The gains came after regional markets settled down following a short-lived sell-off in cryptocurrencies and precious metals.

Santander was trading 3.6% lower after the bank said it would buy U.S. regional lender Webster Bank in a deal worth $12.2 billion. Santander also released its fourth-quarter earnings a day early, which showed net profits of 3.76 billion euros ($4.45 billion) for the three-month period, ahead of consensus estimates of 3.41 billion euros, with the Spanish lender also unveiling a new 5-billion-euro share buyback program.

Novo Nordisk was down 4.9% after its share price plunged 18% in early dealmaking. The company released its results ahead of schedule Tuesday. It warned investors that it sees sales and profit growth declining this year, after it was hit by lower prices in the U.S. and the end of exclusivity for its blockbuster Wegovy and Ozempic weight loss drugs in China, Brazil, and Canada.
Earnings were in focus with Novartis, GSK, Infineon Technologies, Equinor, Credit Agricole, Handelsbanken, Carlsberg, and OMV all posting earnings reports on the day.

Shares in UBS were down 6.3% after Switzerland's largest lender reported a net profit of $1.2 billion in its fourth-quarter results, a 56% year-on-year rise which beat the $919 million forecast by analysts.
